scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. Second week of the year he says after forgetting my name “I’ll remember you, you’re the guy with no soul” and third week “Oh that’s right EverywhereForever, you’re the ginger with no soul”. Most of the class laughed, I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for awhile after that though. Towards the end of the semester though he did it again, and I straight lost my cool and said “It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?” He didn’t say anything, class was quiet and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

In one of my tech classes, a professor made jokes about my appearance on several occasions. The second week of the semester, he forgot my name and said, "I'll remember you; you're the guy with no soul." The third week, he said, "Oh, that's right, 'Everywhere Forever,' you're the ginger with no soul." Most of the class laughed, and I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for a while after that. Toward the end of the semester, he did it again, and I lost my cool. I said, "It's not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?" He didn't say anything, the class was quiet, and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom, came back, and acted like nothing happened. The next day, a kid talked to me outside class and said I was a dick about it, and I just shrugged. I find it arbitrary that my hair color would be the basis for juvenile and insulting remarks in college. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing by reacting the way I did. Is it AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) for how I handled this situation? First, I need to consider the context. The professor is an authority figure, and making jokes about a student's appearance, especially in front of the class, can be hurtful and unprofessional. It's important to address such behavior to maintain a respectful learning environment. On the other hand, losing my cool and confronting the professor in front of the class might have been seen as unprofessional on my part. It could have made the situation more awkward for everyone involved, including myself. I also need to think about the consequences of my actions. By reacting strongly, I might have drawn attention to myself, which I was trying to avoid. Additionally, the fact that another student called me a dick the next day suggests that my reaction might have been perceived negatively by some peers. However, it's also important to stand up for oneself and not tolerate disrespectful behavior. Ignoring the comments might have allowed the professor to continue making such jokes, potentially affecting other students as well. I should also consider alternative ways to address the issue, such as talking to the professor privately after class or reporting the behavior to a higher authority if it continues. These approaches might have been more effective in resolving the issue without causing further embarrassment or conflict. In summary, while standing up for myself is commendable, the way I did it might have been seen as overreacting, especially in a classroom setting where maintaining decorum is important. It's a delicate balance between asserting one's rights and maintaining professionalism. I think I need to reflect on whether my reaction was proportional to the situation and whether there were better ways to handle it. It's also worth considering how my actions might have been perceived by others and whether they align with my personal values and the expectations of the academic environment. Perhaps seeking advice from a counselor or a trusted mentor could provide additional insights and help me navigate this situation more effectively in the future. It's important to find a healthy outlet to express my feelings and address the underlying issues of being made fun of for my appearance. Overall, while I might not be entirely wrong for reacting, there might have been more constructive ways to handle the situation that would have been less confrontational and more aligned with the expectations of a respectful and professional learning environment.
